channel.title: Chicago Trades News
channel.description: A free daily brief for Chicago contractors and trade businesses: new rules, permits, licenses, taxes, pay and big projects, in plain words with the source linked.

item.title: Trade shows ahead: Chicago Build this week, roofing and HVAC shows in January
item.description: Chicago Build runs October 28 and 29 at McCormick Place, with new HVAC, fire safety and AI areas. The Chicago Roofing Contractors Association show is January 20 to 22, 2027 in Oakbrook Terrace, and the AHR Expo for heating and cooling is in Chicago January 25 to 27, 2027. What it means for you: Shows let you see new products and meet suppliers and builders, and some offer seminars and workshops. Chicago Build is this week and lists free tickets, so check its site if you want to go. Source: Plant and Equipment, Chicago Build listing, https://www.plantandequipment.com/exhibitions/chicago-build-28-10-2026

item.title: City Council approves $7.3 million TIF for Altgeld Gardens community center rehab
item.description: The City Council approved $7.3 million in TIF funding and landmark status for the 1945 Up Top Building at 13100 S. Ellis in Altgeld Gardens. By The Hand Club For Kids plans a $25.8 million conversion into a community center. Construction is expected to begin in fall 2026 and finish in fall 2027. What it means for you: A City funded landmark rehab on the Far South Side is starting soon. Check who the general contractor will be and whether the TIF carries City hiring or contracting requirements. Source: Urbanize Chicago, Up Top Building funding, https://chicago.urbanize.city/post/city-council-approves-funding-top-building

item.title: Chicago Fire stadium in The 78 gets its enclosure permit
item.description: The City issued an enclosure permit for McDonald's Park, the privately funded $750 million Chicago Fire FC stadium at 1331 S. Wells in The 78, covering facade and exterior work before interiors start. Pepper Construction, GMA Construction Group and All Construction Group are the joint venture general contractors. Opening is set for the 2028 MLS season. What it means for you: Exterior and then interior trade packages follow an enclosure permit. Check with the joint venture general contractors on how they take subcontractor bids and what prequalification they require. Source: Urbanize Chicago, enclosure permit, https://chicago.urbanize.city/post/enclosure-permit-issued-mcdonalds-park

item.title: Foundry Park breaks ground on the old Lincoln Yards site
item.description: JDL Development and Kayne Anderson Real Estate broke ground on October 21 on Foundry Park, a $3 billion project along the North Branch of the Chicago River. The first phase has more than 700 homes plus shops, parks and underground parking, and a $201.6 million TIF package covers roads, utilities, parks and riverfront work. What it means for you: Phase one is only part of a plan for more than 3,700 homes. Watch for general contractor announcements and ask about subcontract work, from MEP and interiors to landscaping and cleaning. Source: Chicago Sun-Times, Foundry Park breaks ground, https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2026/10/21/foundry-park-developers-break-ground-3-billion-project

item.title: Budget plan would raise Chicago's tax on equipment rentals and cloud software to 20%
item.description: Mayor Johnson's proposed 2027 budget raises the City's personal property lease transaction tax from 15% to 20%, worth about $234 million in 2027. That tax covers rented equipment, software and cloud computing; car leasing would stay at 15%. City Council budget hearings began October 26 and the Council has not voted. What it means for you: If it passes, rented lifts and tools and software subscriptions such as scheduling, invoicing and office apps could cost more. Check which of your bills already carry the Chicago lease tax so you know what would change. Source: WBEZ, head tax returns in the budget plan, https://www.wbez.org/city-hall/2026/10/21/mayor-brandon-johnson-failed-corporate-head-tax-resurrected-proposed-budget

item.title: Budget plan adds 28 City rat crews and 20 vacant lot cleanup crews
item.description: The proposed 2027 budget adds 28 rodent control crews and 20 crews to clear trash from vacant lots, and trims 15,000 more trees a year. It follows a July Inspector General audit that faulted the City for reacting to 311 rat calls instead of preventing them. What it means for you: Pest control firms may hear more from customers about sealing and sanitation, not only bait. The weekly 311 rat counts for every community area are on our free page. Source: WTTW, Johnson's proposed 2027 budget, https://news.wttw.com/2026/10/21/johnson-touts-176b-proposed-budget-2027-let-us-plant-seeds-fair-chicago

item.title: Chicago's 2027 budget plan brings back a per-worker tax on large employers
item.description: Mayor Johnson's proposed 2027 budget includes a tax of $25 a month for each employee at companies with more than 125 workers, which the City expects to raise about $100 million a year. Last year the Council rejected a version at $33 per worker. Council budget hearings began October 26, and the budget needs 26 of 50 votes to pass. What it means for you: The tax only applies above 125 workers, so check your headcount if you are near that line. Larger contractors and cleaning or facility service firms should follow the budget hearings and the vote. Source: WTTW, Johnson's proposed 2027 budget, https://news.wttw.com/2026/10/21/johnson-touts-176b-proposed-budget-2027-let-us-plant-seeds-fair-chicago

item.title: Winter leans mild, with more sleet possible; parking ban starts December 1
item.description: NOAA's December to February outlook leans warmer than normal for the Chicago area with even odds on precipitation, as El Nino strengthens, and an NBC 5 meteorologist says that could mean more days of mixed sleet, snow and freezing rain. The City's overnight parking ban on 107 miles of main streets runs 3 am to 7 am from December 1 to April 1. What it means for you: A milder winter could bring more icy mixed days instead of all snow, though snowstorms can still happen, so watch the forecasts and check your salt supply. Check where your trucks and trailers park overnight before the December 1 ban. Source: NBC Chicago, winter outlook, https://www.nbcchicago.com/weather/el-nino-significantly-impacting-the-chicago-areas-winter-weather-outlook-nws-2/4003406/

item.title: Peoples Gas rate decision due in November; Nicor increase approved
item.description: State regulators approved an $82 million Nicor Gas increase on October 15, far less than the $221 million Nicor asked for. For Peoples Gas, which serves Chicago, state judges recommended cutting its $144 million request to $66 million, and the Illinois Commerce Commission is expected to rule in November. What it means for you: A shop or yard heated by Peoples Gas could see higher bills next year; watch the November ruling. Suburban sites on Nicor should expect the increase on their bills soon. Source: Capitol News Illinois, Nicor rate decision, https://capitolnewsillinois.com/news/partial-win-for-customers-icc-approves-82-million-rate-hike-for-nicor/

item.title: Social Security tax will apply to the first $192,300 of pay in 2027
item.description: The Social Security Administration raised the maximum earnings taxed for Social Security from $184,500 in 2026 to $192,300 in 2027. Medicare tax still has no earnings cap. What it means for you: Owners and crew members who earn more than $184,500 will owe Social Security tax on more of their pay next year. Check that your payroll service and your 2027 estimated tax payments use the new number. Source: Social Security Administration, 2027 fact sheet, https://www.ssa.gov/cola/factsheets/2027.html

item.title: Chicago's updated construction codes are required for permits filed from December 1
item.description: The City Council passed ordinance SO2026-0024930 on June 17, 2026, fully updating Chicago's mechanical, fuel gas, energy and interim fire prevention codes to current model codes, with general changes to the building and rehab codes. The new codes have been optional since October 1 and are required for projects submitted from December 1, 2026, counted from the day the permit fee is paid. What it means for you: Check which jobs will have their permit fee paid on or after December 1, since those must meet the new codes. HVAC contractors should note that all dwelling units now need ducted make up air, and the energy code moves to the 2024 IECC. Source: MAP Strategies, 2026 Chicago construction code updates, https://map-strategies.com/ideas/2026-chicago-construction-code-updates

item.title: Cook County's 2027 budget plan has no property tax increase or new fees
item.description: Board President Toni Preckwinkle's $9.69 billion plan for 2027 closes a $550.8 million gap without a property tax increase, new fees or layoffs. It uses reserves, interest on federal relief money and cuts 50 vacant jobs. What it means for you: County taxes and fees on businesses are not set to rise next year under this plan, but the County Board still has to vote on it. Source: WTTW, Cook County's 2027 budget plan, https://news.wttw.com/2026/10/07/no-tax-hikes-or-layoffs-needed-close-cook-county-s-550m-gap-thanks-budget-magic

item.title: Illinois genetic privacy law expands to biomarker tests; drug testing questions raised
item.description: Public Act 104-0642 extends the Genetic Information Privacy Act to biomarker testing, so employers may not require genetic or biomarker tests as a condition of work or act on the results. A law firm reports the change starts January 1, 2027 and that some employers worry the wording could reach workplace drug tests. What it means for you: If you run pre hire, random or post accident drug tests, ask your testing vendor or lawyer to review the program before January. The law does not mention drug testing by name. Source: Illinois General Assembly, Public Act 104-0642, https://www.ilga.gov/Legislation/PublicActs/PrinterFriendly/104-0642

item.title: 1099s for 2026 payments start at $2,000, not $600
item.description: Under the 2025 federal tax law, businesses send Form 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC only for payments of $2,000 or more made from January 1, 2026, up from $600, with inflation adjustments from 2027. Payment apps file Form 1099-K only above $20,000 and 200 payments. What it means for you: When you send 1099s to subcontractors early next year, the cutoff for 2026 payments is $2,000. Keep collecting a W-9 from every sub. Source: OnPay, 1099 threshold changes, https://onpay.com/insights/1099-reporting-threshold-updates/

item.title: City picks four teams to build 30 two and three flats on the South Side
item.description: The Department of Planning and Development chose 75 Development, Vazquez Housing Development, Blazer Jones and Blueprint Ventures to build 30 small buildings with 62 homes, $27.6 million in all, on City lots in South Chicago and West Englewood. The City would sell each lot for $1 and give up to $150,000 a home, from bond money the City Council still has to approve. What it means for you: Small infill jobs like these suit local trade businesses and small builders. Contact the four developers about sub work, and watch for the Council funding vote that sets the start. Source: Urbanize Chicago, Missing Middle round 4, https://chicago.urbanize.city/post/dpd-announces-round-4-missing-middle-housing-projects

item.title: City contractors and their subs face new conduct certifications; rules due November 24
item.description: An executive order signed August 26 directs the City's chief procurement officer to write rules, due by November 24, 2026, requiring firms seeking City contracts over $250,000 to certify no public integrity, discrimination or wage theft violation in the past five years. Primes must pass matching terms down to their subcontractors. What it means for you: If you work as a sub on City jobs, expect new certification forms from your prime. Make sure your wage and hour records are in order now, since wage theft counts. Source: Skadden, Chicago procurement executive order, https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/10/chicago-executive-order-directs-new-procurement-rule

item.title: From 2027, job ads can ask for a driver's license only when driving is essential
item.description: A change to the Illinois Job Opportunities for Qualified Applicants Act, HB 4758, says that from January 1, 2027 a job posting may require a valid driver's license only when driving is an essential part of the job and a business necessity, and the posting must say why. It covers employers with 15 or more employees and employment agencies. What it means for you: Review every job ad that asks for a driver's license before January. Check that driving is an essential part of that job and that the ad briefly explains why the license is needed. Source: Saul Ewing, Illinois employment law update, https://www.saul.com/insights/blog/illinois-employment-law-update

item.title: New City review for data centers; a temporary pause is proposed
item.description: An executive order signed August 11 sends any data center that needs a new Planned Development through a review of power, water, backup generators, air, noise and neighborhood impact, and orders new air permit and noise rules. Mayor Johnson has also called on the City Council to pause new or expanded data centers until permanent rules are in place, and the Council has not voted on it. What it means for you: Electrical and mechanical contractors chasing data center work in the city should watch for the new air permit and noise rules, due around November 9, and for any Council vote on the pause. Source: Chicago Sun-Times, data center order and proposed pause, https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/08/11/mayor-brandon-johnson-chicago-moratorium-data-centers-new-regulations

item.title: Overtime on 2026 W-2s goes in Box 12, Code TT, for the federal overtime deduction
item.description: The IRS updated its guidance on the federal overtime deduction, worth up to $12,500 a year or $25,000 on a joint return, with a phase out at higher incomes. For 2026, employers report qualified overtime in Box 12 of the W-2 with Code TT, and the 2025 relief is not extended. What it means for you: If you pay hourly crews overtime, set up payroll now to track the federally required overtime premium so January W-2s are right. Only overtime the federal rules require counts, not extra premiums from a union contract or company policy. Source: EY Tax News, IRS 2026 overtime guidance, https://taxnews.ey.com/news/2026-1738-irs-updates-2026-guidance-on-overtime-deduction-with-information-for-employers-and-employees

item.title: Illinois Attorney General gets new powers to investigate employers from January 1
item.description: HB 4725, signed July 31, 2026, lets the Attorney General's Workplace Rights Bureau issue subpoenas, require sworn written answers, inspect non public parts of a business, copy records on site and interview workers, starting January 1, 2027. Knowingly hiding or destroying records under subpoena can be a Class A misdemeanor. What it means for you: Starting January 1, possible violations of Illinois labor and employment laws can lead to state subpoenas, on site inspections and worker interviews without a court order. Check that your timesheets, pay records and worker classification files are complete before January. Source: Amundsen Davis, Attorney General investigation powers, https://www.amundsendavislaw.com/labor-employment-law-update/illinois-attorney-general-expanded-employer-investigation-powers

item.title: Illinois employers with more than 25 workers must pay for jury duty from 2027
item.description: The Governor signed HB 4844 on July 31, 2026, so employers must pay workers their regular rate for time on jury duty starting January 1, 2027. Employers with 25 or fewer employees still only have to give unpaid leave. What it means for you: If you have more than 25 employees, review your handbook and payroll setup for paid jury duty before January. Smaller shops keep giving unpaid time off for jury service. Source: Illinois General Assembly, Public Act 104-0683, https://ilga.gov/Legislation/PublicActs/View/104-0683

item.title: CTA seeks proposals for the Red Line Extension 120th Yard, shop and substation
item.description: The CTA is taking proposals for construction of the Red Line Extension's 120th Yard, shop and substation. Proposals are due November 5, 2026 at 3:30 pm, with the documents on the CTA's Bonfire portal. What it means for you: If you do electrical, mechanical or plumbing work, check the Bonfire documents for the scope and any subcontracting goals, and ask likely prime bidders about joining their teams. Source: City of Chicago vendor search, CTA solicitation C26FI103384111, https://webapps1.chicago.gov/vcsearch/cta/solicitationdetails/C26FI103384111

item.title: Illinois posted new prevailing wage rates for public construction
item.description: The Illinois Department of Labor published new prevailing wage rates for every county and construction trade, in effect from July 15, 2026, from its yearly survey of wages and benefits. Workers on publicly funded construction must be paid at least these rates. What it means for you: If you bid publicly funded construction in Cook County, check the 2026 Cook County rate for your trade on the IDOL prevailing wage page before you bid. Source: Illinois Department of Labor, 2026 prevailing wage rates, https://www.illinois.gov/content/dam/soi/en/web/illinois/iisnewsattachments/32712-071526-7.15.2026-idol-2026-prevailing-wage-rates-published.pdf.pdf

item.title: Chicago's minimum wage is $17.05 an hour
item.description: Chicago's minimum wage rose from $16.60 to $17.05 an hour on July 1, 2026, for employers with four or more workers, and the tipped wage is $12.96. Suburban Cook County is $15.40 and the Illinois minimum stays at $15. What it means for you: Check that helpers, cleaners and entry level crew working in the city get at least $17.05 an hour. Jobs in the suburbs follow the county or state rate. Source: Amundsen Davis, Chicago and Cook County minimum wage increases, https://www.amundsendavislaw.com/labor-employment-law-update/chicago-and-cook-county-minimum-wage-increases-take-effect-july-1-employer-compliance-updates
